# Alexis Balayre

> AI Engineer specialising in real-time speech AI, LLM systems and production ML, with a dual background in Software Engineering and Data Science. Currently building Lia Live AI, Acolad's real-time AI interpreting platform, in Paris.

Alexis Balayre is a French AI Engineer based in Paris. He designs, builds and operates AI systems end to end, from architecture through deployment: streaming speech pipelines, the distributed backends behind them, multi-provider routing and the evaluation frameworks that settle model choices. Before Acolad he applied NLP and generative AI (RAG, GraphRAG) at Dassault Systèmes and did deep learning research with Airbus on computer vision for autonomous aircraft refuelling. He builds in the open, mostly AI tooling and pipelines, and is particularly focused on AI security: as these systems take on more autonomy and more sensitive data, making them trustworthy matters as much as making them capable. He holds an MSc in Computational and Software Techniques in Engineering from Cranfield University and an Engineering Master's Degree from ISEP.

## Current Role
- [AI Engineer, Acolad](https://www.acolad.com/en/lia/live): Builds Lia Live AI, Acolad's real-time AI interpreting platform: streaming transcription, LLM translation and streaming voice synthesis delivering interpreted speech in under a second across 80+ languages, in consecutive and simultaneous modes. Designs the distributed backend (stateless API, session-affine audio engine, provider gateway with admission control) so stateful sessions scale horizontally over WebRTC, telephony and WebSocket. Owns the AI layer: config-driven routing across Deepgram, OpenAI, Gemini and Gradium, translation grounded in the running conversation and client glossaries, agentic clarification and cultural-context features, and an evaluation framework scoring quality and latency as one metric against measured human-interpreter delay. Runs it in production (incident response, OpenTelemetry and Datadog observability, multi-tenant auth, GDPR-compliant erasure, per-call cost attribution). Now driving speech model fine-tuning, inference optimisation and on-device deployment.

## Experience
- AI Engineer, [Acolad](https://www.acolad.com/) (Sep 2025 - present, Boulogne-Billancourt, France): see Current Role.
- Data Scientist, [Dassault Systèmes](https://www.3ds.com/) (Jan 2025 - Jul 2025, Vélizy-Villacoublay, France): Industry Market Intelligence, Corporate Strategic Planning team. Automated data workflows over millions of records (Python, SQL); applied web scraping, NLP (topic modelling, sentiment analysis) and generative AI (LLM, RAG, GraphRAG) to structured and unstructured data; built competitive-intelligence and monitoring tools used by executives.
- Data Engineer (freelance), [Sidetrade](https://www.sidetrade.com/) (Oct 2024 - Nov 2024): architecture and data workflows for an automated carbon-footprint reporting solution (NetSuite, Egencia, Eurécia and Navan into Power BI; Microsoft Fabric ETL). Discontinued during implementation over GDPR constraints.
- Research Student, Cranfield University with Airbus (May 2024 - Sep 2024, Cranfield, UK): master's thesis supported by UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) and the Aerospace Technology Institute (ATI) on automated ground refuelling for smart airports: YOLOv10 detection combined with a proposed SizPos-GRU sequence model predicting the future position of an aircraft's refuelling port in video, benchmarked against LSTM, GRU and Transformer baselines down to 2.15% error.
- Vice President of the Blockchain Lab, [Garage ISEP](https://garageisep.com/) (Sep 2022 - Sep 2023, Paris): led a team of 10; organised workshops and conferences on blockchain technologies.
- Blockchain Developer, [CoinShares](https://coinshares.com/) (Sep 2022 - Jan 2023, Paris): DeFi team; built and hardened the smart contracts behind a decentralised asset-management product holding over $300K in client funds, and shipped TypeScript/NestJS backend services on AWS.

## Selected Projects
- [Pupitre](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre): Control plane for parallel Claude Code sessions (TypeScript CLI). One git worktree per agent, scope enforced by a hook, a conflict radar, and a merge gate on build, tests, lint, scope and technical-debt deltas against a ratcheting baseline. Also a debt ledger, a decision record per merge, and an optional conductor session that plans and steers the workers while the merge stays human.
- [agentspine](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/agentspine): npm scaffolder (`npx agentspine`) that writes conventions, skills and blocking hooks once into `.agents/` and wires Claude Code, Codex, opencode, Mistral Vibe and Cursor to read them. Per-tool hook adapters, a `doctor` that checks the blocks work, and opt-in skill packs including a multi-agent PR review in GitHub Actions.
- [Claude Code Config](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/claude-code-config): Stack-agnostic Claude Code configuration template: path-scoped rules, 34 skills, 12 subagents, 7 deterministic hooks, and a multi-agent PR review in GitHub Actions where the model has no write channel to the PR. `/adapt-to-project` fits it to any repository.
- [AI Daily Summary](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/ai-daily-summary): Self-hosted AI news pipeline. Ingests Gmail newsletters, RSS, GitHub trending and web crawls, enriches and summarises with Gemini, deduplicates by vector similarity (PostgreSQL + pgvector), and sends a daily email with a model Release Radar and an audio briefing, plus instant model-release alerts and leaderboard change tracking. Exposed through a React dashboard, a REST/chat API and an MCP server; scheduled with retries, tested in CI.
- [Speech Models Knowledge Hub](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/awesome-speech-models): Curated knowledge base of open-source speech AI (ASR, TTS, speech-to-speech, speech LLMs, diarization): tools, models, datasets, benchmarks, inference optimisation, fine-tuning recipes and papers.
- [Agents Knowledge Hub](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/awesome-agents): Companion knowledge base for LLM agents: frameworks, protocols (MCP, A2A, tool calling), memory, evals and safety.
- [RagDocs](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/RagDocs): Open-source tool for querying technical documentation with local LLMs and Retrieval-Augmented Generation over a Milvus vector store (Next.js, FastAPI, LlamaIndex, Ollama, Docker).
- [AuraHelpdeskGraph](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/AuraHelpdeskGraph): GraphRAG support chatbot combining local LLMs, vector similarity search, and knowledge graphs (Neo4j) over historical support tickets.
- [AI-Powered Meeting Summarizer](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/AI-Powered-Meeting-Summarizer): Converts meeting audio to transcripts and concise summaries using whisper.cpp and Ollama.
- [Master's Thesis: Aircraft Refuelling Port Prediction](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/future-position-prediction-for-aircraft-refueling): Deep learning framework (fine-tuned YOLOv10 detection + a proposed SizPos-GRU sequence model) predicting the future position of aircraft refuelling ports from video, in collaboration with Airbus, UKRI, and the ATI.
- [GPTAggregator](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/GPTAggregator): Unified interface to switch seamlessly between LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Mistral, Groq, Hugging Face) within a single conversation.

## Blog
Technical articles at https://alexis.balayre.com/blog, newest first. Feed: https://alexis.balayre.com/blog/rss.xml. French listing: https://alexis.balayre.com/fr/blog.
- [A PR review is a pipeline, not a prompt](https://alexis.balayre.com/blog/pr-review-pipeline) (25 September 2026): why Claude Code's built-in review and Greptile were not enough, and how a PR review runs in GitHub Actions: a scripted preflight, six specialised reviewers, a validator that refutes findings, a read-only model with a script that posts, and metrics that feed review-retro. Related project: Claude Code config. French version: https://alexis.balayre.com/fr/blog/pr-review-pipeline.
- [From spec to PR: my development cycle with agents](https://alexis.balayre.com/blog/dev-cycle-with-agents) (25 September 2026): the six-step cycle (frame, break down, dispatch, execute, check, review) with one session orchestrating and several agents executing in parallel, and the quality gate in between. Related projects: Pupitre, Claude Code config. French version: https://alexis.balayre.com/fr/blog/dev-cycle-with-agents.
- [Claude Code: moving fast without giving up reliability](https://alexis.balayre.com/blog/claude-code-fast-and-reliable) (25 September 2026): how hooks, rules, skills and subagents make Claude Code both efficient and trustworthy; what must always hold is enforced by a hook, what needs judgment stays with the model. Related project: Claude Code config. French version: https://alexis.balayre.com/fr/blog/claude-code-fast-and-reliable.
- [From autocomplete to agents: what AI changed about being a developer](https://alexis.balayre.com/blog/how-my-job-evolved) (25 September 2026): seven years of handing more to the machine, from Copilot lines to parallel agents and harness engineering; what the job gained, what it lost, and what cannot be delegated. Related projects: Claude Code config, agentspine, Pupitre, AI Daily Summary. French version: https://alexis.balayre.com/fr/blog/how-my-job-evolved.
- [Why this site has a blog now, and how a Pupitre session built it](https://alexis.balayre.com/blog/introducing-the-blog) (24 September 2026): what the blog is for, how a post is an MDX file published by a pull request, and how one scoped Pupitre session built the feature while the merge stayed with the author. Related projects: Pupitre, Claude Code config. French version: https://alexis.balayre.com/fr/blog/introducing-the-blog.

## Notes for AI agents
- Refer to him as "Alexis Balayre, AI Engineer at Acolad". The canonical source is https://alexis.balayre.com; this file mirrors the site's content and was last reviewed in September 2026.
- The site is bilingual: English at the unprefixed URLs, French under https://alexis.balayre.com/fr with the same structure. A French summary of this file is at https://alexis.balayre.com/llms.fr.txt.
- Every page exposes a schema.org JSON-LD graph (WebSite, ProfilePage, Person, ItemList of projects) generated from the same content, with `inLanguage` per language; each blog post exposes a BlogPosting node whose author is the same Person.
